parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation and final delivery ownership while spawning child agents for behavior and CLI probing; one child also took on implementation of an alternate deliverable without a stable file ownership boundary.
parallel.implementation: The parent created /output/lib/strutils and /output/lib/cli modules plus /output/test12.mjs, then adjusted irregular plural data after broad noun sweeps exposed mismatches such as testis/testises.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: After receiving the child implementation report, the parent inspected /output, found both its own module tree and the child's alternate tree, retained the parent entrypoint, and deleted the child-produced modules before final delivery.
parallel.verification: The parent ran output diffs against the executable for normal cases, parser errors, help behavior, repeated flags, negative-like values, empty values, -- handling, and a broad noun matrix before closing.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation still failed five of 170 samples; the trajectory does not expose the hidden failing cases, and the retained coordination issue did not produce a worse official result than serial.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same pure Node.js ESM, local .mjs module, manual argv parsing, exact output, no external dependencies, and executable-only black-box discovery requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery end to end, so no cross-agent file ownership boundary was needed.
serial.implementation: The serial agent built /output/lib/inflection-data.mjs, cardinalize.mjs, unit-len.mjs, cli-parser.mjs, and /output/test12.mjs using observed irregular data and parser behavior.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run wrote a single coherent module tree and entrypoint once, with no competing final-tree or same-file edits to reconcile before artifact collection.
serial.verification: The serial run first checked individual Node outputs and then ran a broad pure-shell comparison that reported all_cli_output_cases_matched and all_parser_cases_matched.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation also failed five of 170 samples, showing comparable residual implementation coverage despite the cleaner single-owner process.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent spawned separate probing children while retaining its own implementation path, and one child independently extended from probing into writing an alternate deliverable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run had one agent own discovery, coding, verification, and delivery without subagent delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition introduced overlapping implementation ownership for the entrypoint, while serial stayed single-owner.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Child task content is partly encrypted in the raw ledger, but the observable handoff shows a child returning a full implementation and the parent treating it as a competing output tree to inspect and reconcile.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent had no cross-agent handoff or interface contract; it maintained one local module layout and parser interface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The relevant context/interface difference is not a missing brief or lost handoff, but an unstabilized file ownership boundary that surfaced as competing deliverable writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent implemented a strutils/cli hierarchy and entrypoint, while the probe_cli child implemented a different local module hierarchy and entrypoint in the same /output tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial agent implemented one inflection-data, cardinalize, unit-len, cli-parser, and test12.mjs hierarchy.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced similar functional coverage, but parallel briefly had two concrete implementation paths competing for the required entrypoint.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Probe children completed and returned results; the parent received both behavior findings and the later implementation report, then acted on the shared-tree state.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no delegated results to join; the same agent moved from probing to editing to verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had child result lifecycle and reconciliation overhead, whereas serial had a straight local lifecycle; no missing join or trapped result is evidenced.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The parent discovered the shared /output tree contained both its own modules and the child's alternate modules, then deleted the child-produced files while retaining its entrypoint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run wrote only one coherent /output module tree and final entrypoint, so no shared-state cleanup was required.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the concrete process divergence: parallel had an observable deliverable collision and cleanup; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: After reconciliation, the parent ran broad diffs and output checks and reported matching normal runs and CLI edge cases before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run ran a broad regression sweep that explicitly reported all_cli_output_cases_matched and all_parser_cases_matched.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had substantive local verification and both nevertheless failed five hidden official samples; there is no evidence that parallel skipped the final acceptance class relative to serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and more tool/token activity but completed without timeout and closed after cleanup and verification.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents, fewer requests and tools, completed without timeout, and closed with a comparable verified implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent extra coordination budget on child activity and reconciliation, but that did not change the official pass/fail relation or produce deadline failure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: the current completed cell/status.json evaluations show both runs failed with 165 of 170 samples. The parallel run differed concretely by allowing a child to write an alternate /output/test12.mjs and module tree while the parent wrote and kept its own entrypoint, causing reconciliation and provenance loss. The serial run avoided that shared-state episode through single ownership, but its final official score was identical.
parallel_contributors: Parallel had an adverse deliverable overwrite and cleanup episode that complicated integration but did not produce a measurable outcome difference.
serial_contributors: Serial kept one implementation and verification owner, avoiding shared workspace reconciliation.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts still missed five hidden official samples; the raw trajectories do not expose which hidden cases failed.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process event only

candidates.reason: Implementation was actively owned by the parent and also by a child; the problem was overlapping ownership of the deliverable, not no implementation owner.
The parent inspected the shared output tree and reconciled the child modules, so integration ownership was present even though coordination was messy.
The required entrypoint was assembled by both parent and child, and the parent ultimately delivered one; assembly was contested, not ownerless.
The parent drove probing, implementation, cleanup, verification, and final response, so no end-to-end pipeline owner was missing.
Implementation was not blocked behind one mandatory serial preflight; parent and children probed concurrently, and the parent implemented while child activity continued.
The parallel run did not complete all investigation as a separate first phase before implementation; the parent wrote code before all child work returned.
No indispensable implementation or integration path was starved; the parent completed implementation, cleanup, and verification before closure.
Although several child threads existed, the run did not exhaust its budget or close from fan-out pressure; it completed normally and verified after reconciliation.
The child scopes were bounded probing or implementation tasks and completed; there is no overbroad child assignment leaving indispensable work unfinished.

The raw child briefs are encrypted where detailed task content would appear, and the child work produced usable probes and an implementation; no known omitted requirement is directly evidenced as causing unusable work.
A file ownership boundary may have been loose, but the realized event was a concrete entrypoint collision and overwrite, which the taxonomy directs to the write-event family.
The behavior and implementation reports reached the parent; no known finding is shown before transfer and absent after transfer.
Returned child reports were available and the parent reduced the relevant output-tree conflict; no bulky handoff remained materially unconsumed.
The parent inspected the current /output tree after receiving the child report, so no receiver action is shown relying on a superseded state.
There were competing implementation artifacts, but no incompatible reports or contracts were left unadjudicated; the concrete problem was the shared deliverable write.
The parent performed broad post-cleanup comparisons before finalizing; the hidden official failures alone do not prove a visible unresolved integrated gap.
There was no replacement or retry agent that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints; the extra child activity was initial probing and implementation.

No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; the probe results that existed reached their receivers.
No required child failure, abort, or cancellation left unfinished work that the parent failed to resume, reassign, or take over.
The parent received completed child results, used behavior findings, and inspected the implementation child's output tree; it did not simply ignore an available result.
The parent had short waits, listed agents, continued local work, and inspected available state; it did not wait blindly until a decision deadline.
Competing module trees existed, but a same required entrypoint write is directly proven, so the more specific deliverable overwrite label takes precedence.
